subject: Draft for review: QuantaPay + Redwood Inference case study (v0.9) — request for redlines/claim approvals
related_links: Jira: SUP-2444 (latency regression in benchmark window)
body:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@quantapay.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Jun 7, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Draft for review: QuantaPay + Redwood Inference case study (v0.9) — request for redlines/claim approvals

Hi Elena,

As promised, attached is a near-final draft of the QuantaPay case study narrative (v0.9), plus a separate claims/metrics table we’re using to keep the quantified statements consistent.

Two specific asks:
1) Please redline any statements that feel too broad or that you’d want scoped (e.g., “across workloads” vs “for the payments authorization service”).
2) Please confirm what’s OK to publish for: architecture detail, region, and any mention of “peak events” (payroll runs).

Timeline-wise, we’re targeting a copy lock by Wed 6/11 to stay on the planned publish window.

If it’s easier, you can also comment directly in the Google Doc:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1QPay-Redwood-CaseStudy-Draft

Thank you—happy to jump on a 20-min call if that’s faster than async edits.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Product Marketing
Redwood Inference


---

From: Elena Park <elena.park@quantapay.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Jun 7, 2025 at 2:41 PM PT
Subject: Re: Draft for review: QuantaPay + Redwood Inference case study (v0.9) — request for redlines/claim approvals

Hi Soojin,

Thanks—reviewed quickly with Derek and left a first pass of comments in the Doc.

High-level: we’re supportive, but we need to tighten the claim language so it doesn’t read like a blanket guarantee.

Specific redlines / requests:

1) “Cut inference cost per token by ~35%”
- Please scope this to the POC window and to the specific endpoint. Something like:
  “In a 3-week POC on QuantaPay’s payments authorization assistant workload, Redwood reduced estimated cost per 1K generated tokens by ~35% versus our baseline configuration.”
- Also please don’t say “cost per token” without clarifying what’s included/excluded. We need a brief caveat: compute only vs total infra (e.g., excludes upstream retrieval).

2) “p95 latency under 450ms”
- This is only true for our benchmark harness (cached prefix + fixed prompt template). We need:
  - the measurement window
  - prompt shape assumptions (avg input/output tokens)
  - whether streaming is included
- Please remove “consistently” / “at all times.”

3) “Guaranteed throughput during burst events”
- We can’t approve “guaranteed” unless it’s explicitly tied to the capacity reservation terms. Recommend “maintained target throughput” and define the target.

4) Competitive comparisons
- There are a few lines that read like you’re implying a competitor was failing. Please remove vendor names and rephrase as “prior stack.”

5) Architecture diagram
- OK to include high-level components (VPC, gateway, Redwood Dedicated, audit logs), but do not include any internal service names or account-specific network details.

Derek is also asking we add a sentence that the results were for one model + one region (us-east) and may vary by model/sequence length.

Let us know once you’ve made edits and we’ll do a tighter read.

Elena


---

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@quantapay.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, Jun 8, 2025 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Draft for review: QuantaPay + Redwood Inference case study (v0.9) — request for redlines/claim approvals

Elena — this is super helpful (thank you). We can absolutely scope the claims as you outlined.

A couple quick follow-ups so we don’t accidentally over- or under-scope:

1) For cost: are you comfortable with the phrasing “estimated compute cost per 1K generated tokens” (excluding retrieval + app servers)? If yes, we’ll add a footnote in the PDF.

2) For latency: can we publish the benchmark prompt shape (avg input tokens / avg output tokens) as a range? E.g., “~450–900 input tokens” / “~120–250 output tokens.”

3) For burst: we’ll remove “guaranteed.” Would you approve:
   “During a peak-traffic replay representing payroll-run conditions, QuantaPay maintained its target p95 latency and throughput on reserved Dedicated capacity.”

4) Re: model + region: we can add a standard caveat line in the “Results” section. Proposed:
   “Results are based on QuantaPay’s POC workload in us-east using a single model configuration; performance may vary by model, sequence length, and traffic shape.”

We’ll update the draft today and share a clean PDF along with a tracked-changes version.

Best,
Soojin


---

From: Derek Holt <derek.holt@quantapay.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@quantapay.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jun 9, 2025 at 8:17 AM PT
Subject: Re: Draft for review: QuantaPay + Redwood Inference case study (v0.9) — request for redlines/claim approvals

Soojin,

Jumping in—agree with Elena’s notes.

On your questions:
1) “estimated compute cost per 1K generated tokens” is acceptable as long as:
   - you state it’s based on Redwood usage reporting during the POC, and
   - you explicitly exclude: retrieval/embedding pipeline, app servers, and non-Redwood infra.

2) Token ranges: yes, ranges are fine. Please also state that we used a fixed system prompt + tool schema (so people don’t assume arbitrary prompts).

3) Burst language: “peak-traffic replay representing payroll-run conditions” is good. Please avoid “payroll run” as a named business event; keep it generic (“peak traffic”).

4) Caveat line you proposed is fine.

One additional item: please remove “SLA-backed” language unless it’s clearly “Redwood’s SLA” and not “QuantaPay’s.” Legal gets very picky.

Thanks,
Derek Holt
VP, Platform Engineering
QuantaPay


---

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Derek Holt <derek.holt@quantapay.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@quantapay.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jun 9, 2025 at 1:26 PM PT
Subject: Re: Draft for review: QuantaPay + Redwood Inference case study (v0.9) — request for redlines/claim approvals

Derek, thank you—got it.

We’ll implement all of the below in the next revision:
- “estimated compute cost per 1K generated tokens” + explicit inclusions/exclusions
- latency statement scoped to benchmark harness + prompt/token ranges + fixed system prompt/tool schema note
- replace “payroll run” with “peak traffic”
- remove any “SLA-backed” phrasing that could be misread as your SLA
- remove any implied competitive/vendor comparisons

Markus is also updating the measurement notes so we can be precise about the p95 calculation window and whether we’re quoting E2E vs model-time.

Next step: we’ll send v1.0 tomorrow with tracked changes + a short “Claims Approved / Pending” checklist in the email body so it’s easy to sign off.

Best,
Soojin


---

From: Elena Park <elena.park@quantapay.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Derek Holt <derek.holt@quantapay.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 10, 2025 at 4:47 PM PT
Subject: Re: Draft for review: QuantaPay + Redwood Inference case study (v0.9) — request for redlines/claim approvals

Sounds good.

One more request as you revise: in the “Why Redwood” section, please add a sentence clarifying that we selected Dedicated for predictability (reserved capacity + isolation) rather than because Hosted couldn’t meet requirements. We don’t want this to read like Hosted is inherently “not enterprise-ready.”

Also please avoid describing our baseline as “unstable.” It was “variable under burst” / “hard to predict” — different tone.

If you send v1.0 with the checklist, we can turn it in 24–48 hours.

Elena
